parsed.reason: The message states facts flatly without attribution. There is no first-person verb of looking or checking in the opening sentences. The facts arrive as disconnected pieces of information ("Great news! Sunnyside Splash Pad is on Friday..." / "You should also know about the Beaches Rec Centre program..." / "Maya is behind on her routine visit...") with no indication that Hale went and checked these for this family. The message reads like trivia a stranger sent, indistinguishable from an un-sourced list. The closest gesture to attribution comes only at the end ("Want me to keep an eye on all of this for you?") which is too late—the facts have already landed flat, in their own sentences, with no "I found," "I checked," or "I looked" in the lead.
